claims.text: The GI application says Varanasi, Chandauli, Mirzapur and Sonbhadra districts of Uttar Pradesh have been famous for their exclusive soft stone jali work for generations.

quotes.locator: Application 556, description of the goods, p. 84
quotes.quote: Varanasi, Chandauli, Mirzapur, and Sonebha dra of Uttar Pradesh are famous for its exclusive Soft Stone Jali Work since generations.

claims.text: Varanasi's district page says jali, or fretwork, is carved intricately on soft stone and its making requires supreme mastery of masonry and design.

quotes.quote: Jali or fretwork is intricately carved on soft stone and its process requires supreme mastery of masonry and design making.

claims.text: Varanasi soft stone jali pieces are made with an undercut technique from a single piece of stone, without any joints.

quotes.locator: row 10, Varanasi Soft Stone Jali Work
quotes.quote: The Varanasi artisans of Soft stone craft are famous for making the beautiful Jali with undercut technique

quotes.locator: row 10, Varanasi Soft Stone Jali Work
quotes.quote: The uniqueness is that it is created out of a single piece of stone, without any joints.
Its specialty is that unique artefacts are made from under cutwork in a single piece of stone without any joints
These st one are made without any joints.

claims.text: Varanasi's district page says the delicately chiselled jalis, decorated with inlay work, demand time in their making and the skill and creativity of masters.

quotes.quote: Delicately chiseled and decorated with inlay work these elaborately carved jalis demand time in their making along with the skill and creativity of the masters.

claims.text: The GI application says the Varanasi soft stone jali work cluster is the largest concentration of soft stone jali work in India.

quotes.locator: Application 556, geographical area of production, p. 84
quotes.quote: The Varanasi Soft Stone jail work cluster in Uttar Pradesh represents the largest concentration of the soft Stone jail work in India.

claims.text: The soft stone jali work cluster is mainly concentrated in Varanasi district and scattered across Mirzapur, Sonbhadra and Chandauli districts.

quotes.locator: Application 556, geographical area of production, p. 84
quotes.quote: Varanasi Soft Stone jail work cluster is mainly concentrated in Varanasi district and scattered generally all parts of Mirzapur, Sonbhadra, Chandauli district.

claims.text: NABARD places the craft all over Varanasi, in areas such as Ramnagar, Misir Pokhara, Luxa, Sarai Nandan, Lahartara and Bhithari.

quotes.quote: All over Varanasi (U.P.) in the area of Ramnagar, Misir Pokhara, Luxa, Sarai Nandan, Lahartara, Bhithari, etc.

claims.text: The GI application names the Ramnagar, Sonia and Kalimohal areas of Varanasi as places of excellent stone craft artistry.

quotes.quote: Ramnagar,Sonia and Kalimohal areas of Varanasi, is the places to where the instances of excellent artistry of stone craft are found.
Sonia and Kalimohal areas of Varanasi are the places to where the instances of excellent artistry of soft stone craft are to be found

claims.text: Most people of the Ramnagar, Sonia and Kalimohal areas, mainly artisans, earn their livelihood by creating artifacts with stones, the GI application says.

quotes.quote: Ramnagar,Sonia and Kalimohal areas of Varanasi, is the places to where the instances of excellent artistry of stone craft are found. Most people of the areas, mainly the artisans of these areas, ear n their livelihood by creating outstanding artifacts with stones

claims.text: NABARD says the khoria, gorara and anguri stone of the craft is available in Jhansi and Mahoba districts of Uttar Pradesh, the main area being Charkhari.

quotes.quote: Khoria, Gorara, Anguri stone which is available in Jhansi & Mahoba (the main area is Charkhari) district of Uttar Pradesh

claims.text: NABARD says the craftsmanship of the craft is found in Ramnagar, a part of Varanasi district.

quotes.quote: but the craftsmanship is available in Ramnagar (a part of Varanasi district).

claims.text: A NABARD listing gives the base stone of the craft as khoria, gorara and anguri stone.

quotes.quote: The base material of stone craft / shape stone is Khoria, Gorara, Anguri stone

claims.text: The GI application gives soapstone as the base material of Varanasi stone craft, with marble and gorara used occasionally.

quotes.locator: Application 556, method of production, raw materials, p. 87
quotes.quote: The base material of stone craft in Varana si is soapstone and occasionallymarble and gorara.

claims.text: Soft stones or soapstone are excavated from open mines, and large boulders are carried to workshops where craftsmen give them the desired shapes and sizes.

quotes.quote: Soft Stones/Soap Stone are excavated from open mines. Large sized boulders are carried to the workshops where they are given desire d shapes and sizes by skilled and seasoned craftsmen.

claims.text: The GI application says soft stone has no homogeneity of colour, tint and texture, and two pieces from the same block are never alike.

quotes.quote: It is interesting to note, ther e is no homogeneity of color, ti nt and texture in soft stone.
Two pieces taken out, even from the same block of soft stone, are never alike.

claims.text: Varanasi soft stone craft is famous for creating designs with the natural veins of the stone.

quotes.quote: Soft Stone is an auspicious craft of Vara nasi and is famous for the creating designs with the natural veins of the stone.
The soft stone jali work is a unique craft of the state recognised by the intricate carvings on the natural veins of the stone.

claims.text: The GI application says soapstone is the softest form of limestone and easy to work on, so any kind of carving can be done by hand on soft stone.

quotes.quote: While Marble is the hardest form of limestone, Soap Stone is the softest and is easy to work on.
For this specific property of it, any kind of carving can be done by hand on soft stone.

claims.text: The GI application calls soft stone one of the kinds of limestone found in the country, marble being the hardest form, and NABARD calls it one of the country's softest limestones.

quotes.quote: Soft Stone is the most appealing of the ki nds of lime stones found in the country.
While Marble is the hardest form of limestone, Soap Stone is the softest and is easy to work on.
The soft stone used in this craft is one of the softest limestones found in the country.

claims.text: Mineral references describe soapstone, or steatite, in general as a very soft rock composed mainly of the mineral talc, a hydrated magnesium silicate.

quotes.quote: A very soft rock composed primarily of the mineral talc. Steatite, commonly called soapstone, is composed of hydrated magnesium silicate.
Soapstone is composed primarily of talc and shares many physical properties with that mineral.

claims.text: Geology.com describes soapstone in general as a metamorphic rock composed mainly of talc, with varying amounts of chlorite, pyroxenes, micas, amphiboles, carbonates and other minerals.

quotes.quote: Soapstone is a metamorphic rock that is composed primarily of talc, with varying amounts of chlorite, pyroxenes, micas, amphiboles, carbonates, and other minerals.

claims.text: The GI application says soapstone is relatively soft because of its high talc content, talc having a value of 1 on the Mohs hardness scale.

quotes.quote: Soapstone is relatively soft because of its hi gh talc content, talc having a definitional value of 1 on the Mohs hardness scale.

claims.text: According to the GI application, soapstone has no fixed hardness because its talc content varies from as little as 30% in architectural grades to as much as 80% in carving grades.

quotes.quote: There is no fixed hardness fo r soapstone because the amount of talc it contains varies widely, from as little as 30% for architectural grades such as those used on countertops, to as much as 80% for carving grades.

claims.text: According to the GI application, common non-architectural soapstone can just barely be scratched with a fingernail, a hardness of 2.5 on the Mohs scale.

quotes.quote: Common, non-architectural grades of soapstone can just barely be scratched wi th a fingernail and are thus considered to have a hardness of 2.5 on the Mohs scale.

claims.text: The GI application adds that a rock which cannot be scratched with a knife blade, of hardness 5.5, is not soapstone.

quotes.quote: If a candidate rock cannot be scratched with a knife blade (hardness of 5.5), it is not soapstone.

claims.text: CAMEO notes that native steatite in general is so soft a fingernail can scratch it, but baking dehydrates and hardens the stone.

quotes.quote: Native steatite is so soft it can be scratched with a fingernail, but baking results in dehydration and hardening of the stone.

claims.text: In general, the name soapstone comes from the rock's soapy feel and its softness.

quotes.quote: Its name is derived from its "soapy" feel and softness.
Soft er grades may feel soapy when touched, hence the name.

claims.text: Geology.com says fine-grained soapstone in general works best for highly detailed carvings, and minerals other than talc and the level of metamorphism can influence its hardness.

quotes.quote: Soapstone with a fine grain size works best for highly detailed carvings. The presence of minerals other than talc and the level of metamorphism can influence its hardness.

claims.text: Mineral references say soapstone in general shares many physical properties with talc: it is soft and very easy to carve, nonporous, heat resistant and resistant to acids and alkalis.

quotes.quote: Soapstone is composed primarily of talc and shares many physical properties with that mineral.
soft and very easy to carve nonporous nonabsorbent low electrical conductivity heat resistant high specific heat capacity resistant to acids and alkalis
Insoluble in water, cold acids or alkalis

claims.text: Crosthwaite's monograph recorded that Bundelkhand produced soapstone, or steatite, found in Lalitpur and the south-west corner of Hamirpur.

quotes.quote: Bundelkhand also produces soap-stone (steatite) which is found in Lalitpur and the south-west oorner of Hamirpur.

claims.text: Crosthwaite judged that the best soapstone carving came from Agra, the soft and tenacious stone lending itself readily to the chisel.

quotes.quote: The best soap-stone carving, however, undoubtedly comes from Agra. The stone, being soft and tenacious, lends itself readily to the chisel.

claims.text: The GI application numbers the main techniques 1 cutting, 2 turning, 3 jali making, 4 carving, 5 buffing and 6 polishing.

quotes.quote: The main techniques are following below:- 1. Cutting 2. Turning 3. Jali Making 4. Carving 5. Buffing GI Journal No. 101 87 November 28, 2017 6. Polishing

claims.text: The GI application lists chisels of different sizes, stone rasps or rifflers and sandbags as tools, with goggles or safety glasses for protection.

quotes.quote: Different size of Chisel, stone rasps(rifflers), sandbags and for personal protection Goggles or safety glasses

claims.text: The GI application says the craftsperson working on sajjar pathar first studies the natural design contained in the stone selected for the work.

quotes.quote: The crafts person while worki ng on the sajjar pathar first studies the natural design contains in the stone selected to work upon.

claims.text: The stone is then shaped very carefully into the form of the desired figure with chisel and hammer.

quotes.quote: Th e shaping is done thereafter very carefully with chisel and hammers.
This slab is now converted in the form of the desired figure with a hammer and a chisel.

claims.text: The stone is smoothed by rubbing it with sandpaper or a file.

quotes.quote: The stone is smoothened by rubbing with sand papers or file.
Sandpaper is used to smoothen the stone

claims.text: Craftsmen sprinkle water on the stone while they work because friction from constant chiselling makes the tools heat up.

quotes.quote: The craftsmen, sprinkle water on the stone during the course of their work because of the friction generated due to the constant chiseling away of the unwanted
material results in the tools heating up.
Water is sprinkled repeatedly to avoid heat generation.

claims.text: The dimensions of the figure are marked on a stone slab, and extra edges are removed from the slab by beating with a hammer.

quotes.quote: Dimensions of the figure to be manufactured are marked on a stone slab. Extra edges are removed from the slab by beating with a hamm er.

claims.text: Big pieces of stone are cut vertically into smaller slabs, rough sketches are made on them, and the article is taken out with a saw.

quotes.quote: Big pieces of stone are cut vertically into smaller slabs, and rough sketches are ma de on it. The article is taken out from the slab with the aid of a saw.

claims.text: Jali making then starts with very fine iron tools, which make various very small holes at various places in the piece.

quotes.quote: After that with the support of very fine iron tools, Jali making process has started and making the variou s very small holes in the various places of the craft

claims.text: The artisan inserts an iron tili inside and removes the extra stone of the first cut, repeating this several times from various angles.

quotes.quote: then the artisan start insert ing the iron Tili inside and removing the extra stone pieces from first cut step and the sa me process has repeated several times from various angles

claims.text: When only a small piece of stone is left inside, the artisan shapes and carves the inside figure, which completes a jali made by one cut.

quotes.quote: then after that only a sm all piece of stone will available in the inside of the craft, then the artisan start the shap ing and carving work within the inside figure.
This is the first Jali making process by one cut.

claims.text: Varanasi artisans make jali in up to 3 cuts, an elephant within an elephant within an elephant being a piece of 3-cut jali work.

quotes.quote: In Varanasi, the artisans are making up to 3 cuts; means 3 different steps of Jali making like - Elephant - within elephant - within elephant is a example of 3 cut Jali work of a elephant piece as a craft.
the artisans are making this jali work in a delic ate manner in one cut, two cut and up to three cut

claims.text: The same jali process is adopted for globes, birds, lions, various other animal figures and decorative items.

quotes.quote: The same type of process has adopted in Jali work in Glob, Birds figure, Li on, various type of animal figures including decorative items.

claims.text: The GI application calls making a jali within a jali in a single piece of stone, with the support of small tools, a unique feature.

quotes.quote: Making the Jali within Jali in a single piece of stone is a unique feature with exclusiv e way of working with the su pport of small tools is much popular across the world.

claims.text: Minor carvings of different types are done with a pointed chisel, and a hammer and chisel do further smoothening.

quotes.quote: Different type of Minor carvings is done by pointed chisel. A hammer and chisel do further smoothening.

claims.text: Before carving, the stone is kept overnight in boiling water and treated chemically, which smoothens and whitens its surface.

quotes.quote: Befo re carving the stone is kept in boiling water overnight and treated chemically.
This smoothens and whitens the surface of th e stone.

claims.text: Polishing for the final finishing is done with sand or carborundum pieces.

quotes.quote: Polishing is done for the final finishing with sand or carborundum pieces.

claims.text: Several of the carved pieces are painted, and others are fitted with looking glasses and brass fittings.

quotes.quote: Se veral of the carved artifacts are painted. Others are fitted with the looking glasses, brass fittings etc.

claims.text: Finishing is done in a variety of ways, from sandpapering to polishing with multani mitti or clay, oil and cloth.

quotes.quote: Fini shing is accomplished in a variety of ways from sand-papering, polishing with multani-mitti or clay, oil and cloth.

claims.text: An outline is drawn on stone already cut to size, and once it is incised the final figure is brought out by removing the unwanted portions.

quotes.quote: An outline is drawn on hard or soft stone wh ich is already cut to the appropriate size.
Once the outline is incised indicating the sh ape, the final figure is brought out by removing the unwanted portions.

claims.text: Harder stones are worked by chiselling out the extra material, while softer stones are scraped out with a sharp flat-edged iron tool.

quotes.quote: While for the harder stones this is done by chiseling out the extra material, with softer stones. This is done by scraping out the same with a sharp flat-edged iron tool.

claims.text: The crafted articles are buffed for smoothness, and some are also lacquered to impart sheen and glow.

quotes.quote: The articles thus crafted, are buff shed for smoothness. Some are also lacquered to impart sheen and glow.

claims.text: Crosthwaite wrote that, except for Agra and Muttra, more good stone carving was to be seen at Benares than in any other district of the provinces.

quotes.quote: Benares. - With the exception of Agra and Muttra; there is more good stonecarving to be seen at Benares than in any other district of these Provinces.

claims.text: The GI application cites H. S. Crosthwaite's Monograph on Stone Carving in the United Provinces as published in 1905.

quotes.quote: According to the book Monograph on Stone carving in united province by H.S. CROSTHWAITE published in 1905

claims.text: The title page of H. S. Crosthwaite's monograph on stone carving in the United Provinces gives Allahabad and the year 1906.

quotes.quote: UNITED PROVINCES. BT H. S. CROSTHWAITE, I.C.S. ALLAHABAD:
1906. PREFACE. This monograph has been written in accordance with G. O.

claims.text: Writing of stone carving in general, Crosthwaite recorded that most workmen in Benares and Mirzapur were Gonds, Mullahs, Telis, Barhais, Kunjrae and other similar castes.

quotes.quote: In Benares and Mirzapur most of the workmen are Gonds, Mullahs, Telis, Barhais, Kunjrae and othe> similar castes.

claims.text: Crosthwaite wrote that nearly all stone carving in Benares was expended on religious edifices, in a city where caste distinctions were specially strict.

quotes.quote: In Benares this is explained by the faot that caste distinctions are specially strict in that city, and that nearly all thp stone-oarving is expended on religious edifices

claims.text: Crosthwaite wrote that jali work in the United Provinces was done in marble and sandstone and was almost entirely used for architectural ornament.

quotes.quote: Jdh work in these provinces is done is marble and sandstone.
Jdli work is almost entirely used for arohiteotural ornament

claims.text: Varanasi's district page says jali work can be seen in Varanasi on forts, zamindari homes, places of worship and ancient monuments, all a testimony to its antiquity.

quotes.quote: In Varanasi the jali craft work can be seen on forts, zamindari homes, places of worship and ancient monuments all of which are a testimony tr its antiquity.

claims.text: The GI application calls soft stone one of the oldest craft clusters in Varanasi, itself one of the oldest clusters of various crafts.

quotes.quote: Varanasi is the one of the oldest clusters of various crafts and soft stone being one of the oldest cluster present in Vara nasi.

claims.text: NABARD says the craft now faces reluctance due to a lack of modern infrastructure to speed up production.

quotes.quote: The rich tradition of this craft carried forward for generations now faces reluctance due to a lack of modern infrastructure to speed up production.

claims.text: NABARD names a lack of copyright knowledge as another stumbling block, resulting in the infiltration of inauthentic products.

quotes.quote: In addition, lack of copyright knowledge is another stumbling block resulting in the infiltration of inauthentic products.

claims.text: Besides articles that catch the fancy of local people and tourists, the artisans create exclusive items for decoration in homes, the GI application says.

quotes.quote: Apart from creating different articles that catch the fancy of the local people and the tourists as well, the artisans create exclusive items that are placed in the trendy house to suit the decorative purpose.

claims.text: NABARD's listing says Varanasi soft stone artisans are famous for making the very popular 'Elephant within the Elephant' art pieces.

quotes.quote: The Varanasi artisans of Soft stone craft are famous for making the beautiful Jali with undercut technique and making the very popular 'Elephant within the Elephant' art pieces by their unique human skill
For example, inside an elephant made of the same stone, another elephant, another elephant or any other animal, bird or figure is engraved inside it.
The most popular item is the undercut elephant.

claims.text: Artisans make decorative pieces in the forms of birds, animals, balls and statues, with traditional motifs carved in the jaali and on its upper side.

quotes.quote: They are making various types of decorative pieces using various forms of Birds, Animal, Ball, Statues with variety of carving and different type of traditional motifs in Jaali and upper side on the jaali.

claims.text: Statues of religious significance are also made with this technique, and such sculptures would be embedded with semi-precious stones and shell work.

quotes.quote: Statues of religious significance are also made using this technique. To further enhance the beauty of these sculptures they would be embedded with semi-precious stones and shell- work.

claims.text: The GI application says the stone craft of Varanasi in general includes marble boxes, wall plates, table tops, coasters, ashtrays, paperweights and candleholders of different sizes.

quotes.quote: The stone craft of Varanasi in clude marble boxes, wall plat es, table tops, coasters, and ashtrays, paperweights, and candleholders, of different sizes

claims.text: Besides temple carvings and sculptures of deities, soft stone work makes items such as table tops, boxes, coasters, trays, carved panels, tiles, paperweights, pen stands and models of historical buildings.

quotes.quote: Of soft stone working is not only restricted to ornate carvings on temples or sculptures of deities, but also used in making items like carved panels, tiles, paper we ights, pen stands, models of historical buildings, sculptures of animals and humans etc.
Today small items of utility and decor are also produced such as table tops, boxes, coasters, trays,etc.
From traditional designs, they have now expanded their portfolio to contemporary products such as tiles, paperweights, pen stands, and more.

claims.text: The GI application describes soft stone craft dolls figuring mythological characters, which were meant to delight and to inculcate traditional values.

quotes.quote: The se soft stone craft dolls, figuring mythological characters, were meant to delight and inculcate traditional values as well.

lede.text: Varanasi soft stone jali work is fretwork carved intricately on soft stone, which the GI application says has been famous for generations in Varanasi, Chandauli, Mirzapur and Sonbhadra districts of Uttar Pradesh.
Its pieces are made with an undercut technique from a single piece of stone without any joints, and its very popular 'Elephant within the Elephant' pieces carve one elephant inside another.
The GI application gives soapstone as the base material, with marble and gorara used occasionally, while a NABARD listing names khoria, gorara and anguri stone.
Banaras Handicraft Development Society applied in 2016 to register the craft as a geographical indication, application 556, which the registry lists as registered.

sentences.text: Crosthwaite's monograph on stone carving in the United Provinces judged that, except for Agra and Muttra, more good stone carving was to be seen at Benares than in any other district.
Crosthwaite wrote that jali work in the United Provinces was done in marble and sandstone and was almost entirely used for architectural ornament.
Crosthwaite wrote that stone fretwork, then the chief beauty of Muttra carving, was originally introduced by the Muhammadans at Agra and Fathpur-Sikri.

Crosthwaite wrote that the modern Hindu carving at Benares had not much jali work or pierced stonework, while Varanasi's district page says jali work can be seen on its forts, zamindari homes, places of worship and ancient monuments, a testimony to its antiquity.
NABARD says the work was once widely visible in places of worship, forts and ancient sculptures, and the GI application calls soft stone one of the oldest craft clusters in Varanasi.
Crosthwaite recorded that Bundelkhand produced soapstone, found in Lalitpur and the south-west corner of Hamirpur, and judged that the best soapstone carving came from Agra.
The GI application cites Crosthwaite's monograph as published in 1905, its preface is dated July 1905, and its title page gives 1906.

Writing of stone carving in general, Crosthwaite recorded that most workmen in Benares and Mirzapur were Gonds, Mullahs, Telis, Barhais, Kunjrae and other similar castes, while Global InCH says Varanasi's stone-carving artisans belong to a community called the raidas.
The GI application numbers the main techniques as cutting, turning, jali making, carving, buffing and polishing.

The dimensions of the figure are marked on a stone slab, big stones are cut vertically into smaller slabs, and the article is taken out with a saw and shaped into the desired figure with chisel and hammer.
Jali making starts with very fine iron tools that make various very small holes, and then an iron tili inserted inside removes the extra stone of the first cut from various angles.
When only a small piece of stone is left inside, the artisan carves the inside figure, and Varanasi artisans make jali in up to 3 cuts.
Before carving, the stone is kept overnight in boiling water and treated chemically, which smoothens and whitens its surface.
Craftsmen sprinkle water on the stone because friction from constant chiselling makes the tools heat up.
The articles are buffed for smoothness, some are lacquered, and polishing is done with sand or carborundum, multani mitti or clay, oil and cloth.
The GI application gives soapstone as the base material, with marble and gorara used occasionally, while a NABARD listing names khoria, gorara and anguri stone.
Soft stones or soapstone are excavated from open mines, and large boulders are carried to workshops.
The GI application says soft stone has no homogeneity of colour, tint and texture, and two pieces from the same block are never alike.
The GI application says soapstone is the softest form of limestone and easy to work on, so any kind of carving can be done by hand on soft stone.
Mineral references say soapstone in general is soft and very easy to carve, nonporous, heat resistant and resistant to acids and alkalis.

Mineral references describe soapstone, or steatite, in general as a very soft rock composed mainly of talc, a hydrated magnesium silicate, while the GI application and NABARD describe the soft stone as a kind of limestone.
Geology.com describes soapstone in general as a metamorphic rock composed mainly of talc, with varying amounts of chlorite, pyroxenes, micas, amphiboles, carbonates and other minerals.
The GI application says soapstone is relatively soft because of its high talc content, talc having a value of 1 on the Mohs hardness scale.
According to the GI application, soapstone has no fixed hardness because its talc content varies from as little as 30% in architectural grades to as much as 80% in carving grades.
The GI application gives common non-architectural soapstone a hardness of 2.5, just barely scratched by a fingernail, and CAMEO notes that baking dehydrates and hardens steatite in general.
In general, the name soapstone comes from its soapy feel and softness, and fine-grained soapstone works best for highly detailed carvings.
The GI application describes the Varanasi soft stone jali work cluster as the largest concentration of soft stone jali work in India.
The cluster is mainly concentrated in Varanasi district and scattered across Mirzapur, Sonbhadra and Chandauli districts.
NABARD places the craft all over Varanasi, in areas such as Ramnagar, Misir Pokhara, Luxa, Sarai Nandan, Lahartara and Bhithari, and the GI application names the Ramnagar, Sonia and Kalimohal areas.
NABARD says the craftsmanship is found in Ramnagar, while its khoria, gorara and anguri stone is available in Jhansi and Mahoba districts, the main area being Charkhari.
The registry gives the geographical area of the indication as Uttar Pradesh.

Banaras Handicraft Development Society applied on 25 July 2016 to register the craft as a geographical indication, application 556, facilitated by the Banaras Handicraft Development Industrial Cooperative Society Limited and the Human Welfare Association.
The application was advertised as accepted in Geographical Indications Journal 101 dated 28 November 2017.
The registry record gives certificate number 315 with a certificate date of 28 March 2018, its document list dates the certificate 18 May 2018, and NABARD says the craft was recognised in 2016.
The registry record lists 185 authorised users and gives the registration as valid up to 24 July 2026.
Most people of the Ramnagar, Sonia and Kalimohal areas, mainly artisans, earn their livelihood by creating artifacts with stones, the GI application says.
NABARD says the craft faces a lack of modern infrastructure to speed up production and a lack of copyright knowledge resulting in the infiltration of inauthentic products.
ANI reported in March 2022 that families in Varanasi's stone carving business had fallen from about three to four thousand to 300 to 250, with neither artisans nor businessmen making profits.
People in Varanasi's stone art business told ANI that the closed Mahoba mine had been where they used to get cheap stones, and that their products are exported to America and Canada.
NABARD's listing says Varanasi soft stone artisans are famous for making the very popular 'Elephant within the Elephant' art pieces.
The same jali process is adopted for globes, birds, lions, various other animal figures and decorative items.
Varanasi soft stone craft is famous for creating designs with the natural veins of the stone.
Statues of religious significance are also made with this technique, and such sculptures would be embedded with semi-precious stones and shell work.
Besides temple carvings and sculptures of deities, soft stone work makes items such as table tops, boxes, coasters, trays, tiles, paperweights and pen stands.
NABARD says artisans make decorative pieces in the forms of birds, animals, balls and statues, with traditional motifs in the jaali and on its upper side.
